Turning Data into Science
Bring It Back to Kerbin

The most obvious way to generate Science is through activities. At its simplest this involves observations \nby the crew (crew or EVA reports), and works its way up through performing experiments all the way to \nprocessing data in a lab.

These involve the use of science parts to perform 
experiments. These tend to generate more data, 
but you do need to keep the subject in mind.

For example you won't get any siesmology readings 
if your vessel is in space.
A simple action the crew perform as required. Once \nyou have done these you will rarely get any reward \nfor repeating them with the same subject.
Experimenting for Profit
Experiment Reports
Crew/EVA Reports

You can process your reports in the lab if there are scientists aboard your vessel. They will slowly process 
the data into Science points (using lots of EC), before returning the report to you so you can deliver it to 
Kerbin. The number and level of the scientists aboard affects how quickly the report data is converted 
into Science.

One other way to use the data you generate is with the MPL-LG-2 Mobile Processing Lab. This behemoth \nof a part is something you will have to work up to in career, but the benefits can be substantial.
Another added side-effect is that the lab can "clean" Goo and Science Jr modules so they can be reused \nafter their data has been extracted.
Processing Data in Situ

To transmit the report you will need a communications 
antenna and enough EC to send the data. If you do not have 
enough EC to send the data in one go then you can choose to 
receive diminished returns (via the "Allow Partial" mode) or 
have the report returned and try again ("Require Complete" 
mode - this is the default).

As usual there are a range of parts, and these have varied 
capabilities regarding data throughput and EC required.
Transmitting the report means you will get Science \nwithout having to fly all the way home, but you will \nonly get a percentage of the recovery value.
Another downside is that no matter how many times \nyou transmit the same experiment/subject combo \nyou cannot extract all the possible science.
Another way to get the data back to Kerbin is by \ntransmitting it.
